hero.headline: Fort Pierce community rallies to save rare deep-sea coral reef as federal ruling looms
hero.body:
Dozens of community members gathered at the Blake Library in Martin County to rally support for the Oculina Bank, a rare deep-water coral reef located just off the coast of Fort Pierce. The reef, found nowhere else on Earth, sits hundreds of feet below the surface and thrives in deep, dark waters unlike most coral that needs shallow sunlight to survive. The reef is home to more than 2,000 marine species.

The rally followed a January vote by the federally-appointed South Atlantic Marine Fishery Council to reopen more than 24 square nautical miles of the reef to shrimp trawling, an area larger than the island of Manhattan. Scientists say trawling destroyed as much as 90 percent of the reef before federal protections were put in place decades ago. Dr. Grant Gilmore, a scientist who previously dived the reef, told the crowd that fish need the coral reef for habitat and food. Mark Perry, Executive Director of the Florida Oceanographic Society, said he was devastated by the council's decision to amend protections that had been in place for decades.

Both scientists urged the public to help save the reef, noting that corals are in trouble worldwide and none should be destroyed. Perry said the corals grow very slowly and have been there for a long time. The council's vote came despite tens of thousands of petition signatures opposing the move.

The proposal is now with NOAA, which will make the final decision. The agency is expected to release draft rules within the coming months, giving the public one more opportunity to weigh in before officials decide whether to move forward. Activists are urging residents to write letters to their congressman and others who might influence the decision to protect the reef.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged with attempted murder after setting fire with 62-year-old inside
cards.teaser: A Port St.
cards.body:
A Port St. Lucie woman is facing attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while a 62-year-old woman was trapped inside the room Sunday night. Michelle Picard, 26, was arrested following the incident at a home in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard.

Port St. Lucie police responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire around 9:05 p.m. Sunday. The victim discovered smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and found Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames before the woman managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911.

Officers detained Picard outside the residence, but she resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to receive treatment for smoke inhalation. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and released. The victim was also hospitalized for treatment of injuries sustained during the incident. Fire investigators determined the blaze was intentionally set.

Picard faces charges of attempted murder, arson and resisting arrest without violence. Her total bond is set at $510,000. The American Red Cross is assisting the victim with temporary housing and support services. Port St. Lucie police emphasized this was an isolated domestic incident and there is no ongoing threat to the community.

cards.headline: Florida school bus driver arrested after second student makes allegations
cards.body:
A Florida school bus driver has been arrested following allegations from a second student, according to Treasure Coast News. The arrest marks an escalation in an ongoing investigation involving student safety concerns on school transportation routes.

The driver's arrest came after a second student came forward with allegations, prompting law enforcement action. The incident raises concerns for parents and school administrators across the Treasure Coast about the screening and oversight of individuals responsible for transporting students to and from school each day.

School bus drivers in Florida are required to undergo background checks and regular training as part of their employment. The arrest highlights the importance of these safeguards and the role that students and parents play in reporting concerning behavior. School districts typically place employees on administrative leave pending the outcome of criminal investigations.

The case remains under investigation by local law enforcement. Parents with concerns about school transportation safety are encouraged to contact their school district transportation departments directly.

cards.headline: Florida Legislature Approves Property Tax Cut Plan for November Ballot
cards.body:
The Florida Legislature has approved a property tax cut proposal backed by Governor Ron DeSantis that will go before voters in November. The measure, which passed despite objections from local government leaders, would change how property taxes are assessed across the state.

Jacksonville-area leaders joined officials from other regions in voicing concerns about the proposal. Local government representatives worry the tax cuts could reduce revenue streams that fund essential services at the city and county level. The property tax reduction plan represents a significant shift in how Florida handles property taxation, requiring voter approval through a constitutional amendment on the November ballot.

The DeSantis-backed plan aims to provide tax relief to Florida property owners amid ongoing concerns about housing affordability and rising property values. Supporters argue the cuts will put money back in the pockets of homeowners and businesses across the state. The measure would need to pass with 60 percent voter approval to become part of the Florida Constitution.

Florida voters will make the final decision this November on whether to approve the property tax changes. If passed, the amendments would affect how local governments fund schools, public safety, infrastructure, and other services that rely on property tax revenue. The debate reflects ongoing tension between state-level tax policy and local government funding needs, an issue that has played out repeatedly in recent Florida legislative sessions as property values have increased statewide.

cards.headline: North Miami man arrested after attempted armed kidnapping at Port St. Lucie church
cards.teaser: A 64-year-old man was arrested Sunday evening after allegedly attempting to kidnap a 74-year-old woman at gunpoint in a First United Methodist Church parking lot in Port St. Lucie.
cards.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami faces multiple felony charges following the incident at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard Sunday morning. The attempted kidnapping unfolded around 10:49 a.m. in the church parking lot, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached the 74-year-old woman despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her.

Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim through the parking lot and physically restraining her.

Zamora was located and arrested without incident Sunday evening at a residence in Hialeah by Port St. Lucie Police and U.S. Marshals. The investigation revealed Zamora is a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Zamora faces five felony charges, including attempted kidnapping with a firearm, aggravated assault and battery of a person over 65. He is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on a $745,000 bond.

cards.headline: Martin County Sheriff announces arrests in hardware store theft ring that hit Stuart, Fort Pierce and 40 other stores
cards.teaser: The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced arrests in Operation Hammer Time, a retail theft ring that burglarized hardware stores across Martin, Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties. At least 40 stores across 13 counties were hit, with roughly $500,000 in stolen goods.
cards.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced arrests in a retail theft ring that targeted hardware stores across Martin, Palm Beach and St. Lucie counties from December 2025 to April 2026. Major Ruben Romero said Johnny Batista, 19, Roberto Hernandez-Castro, 39, and Roberto Aldana-Ferrera, 31, were all involved in the burglaries dubbed Operation Hammer Time. At least 40 stores across 13 counties were burglarized, with roughly $500,000 worth of property stolen, plus additional damage to stores.

According to the Martin County Sheriff's Office, hardware stores in Stuart, Fort Pierce, Jupiter, Lake Worth, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, and West Palm Beach were among those targeted, as well as stores in Broward County. The crews used a sledgehammer or other blunt object to smash glass and often completed the thefts within minutes, before police arrived or alarms were triggered. The stolen goods were taken back to Miami-Dade County, where the suspects lived, to be sold.

Aldana-Ferrera is in custody in Georgia, Batista was arrested in February for a vehicle theft and is in Martin County Jail, and Hernandez-Castro has a warrant out for his arrest. A fourth suspect, Maikell Fleitas, is deceased. Investigators say Batista is connected to the first known theft at Sewell Hardware in Stuart in December 2025. The suspects face charges of racketeering, burglary over $1,000 in damage while masked, burglary of an occupied structure and burglary of an unoccupied structure.

cards.headline: Heiress donates land adjacent to Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve to block development
cards.body:
An heiress is purchasing and donating land in Hobe Sound to prevent future development and protect environmentally sensitive habitat. The land sits adjacent to the Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve, a critical natural area that protects rare scrub habitat along the northern Treasure Coast.

The acquisitions represent a conservation strategy to permanently protect open space near the preserve from residential or commercial development. By purchasing properties and transferring them to public or conservation ownership, the heiress is effectively removing development rights that would otherwise allow construction in the area.

The Hobe Sound Scrub Preserve protects one of the last remaining examples of sand pine scrub habitat in Martin County, home to threatened and endangered species including the Florida scrub jay and gopher tortoise. Land adjacent to the preserve faces development pressure as buildable parcels become scarcer in the rapidly growing Hobe Sound area.

The donated parcels will expand the protected buffer around the preserve, ensuring wildlife corridors remain intact and preventing future encroachment. Conservation organizations often work with private donors to secure strategically important parcels that connect or expand existing preserves, creating larger protected landscapes for native species and public recreation.

cards.headline: Vero Beach approves $190,000 sidewalk project on Iris Lane
cards.teaser: The city of Vero Beach has approved a $190,000 sidewalk construction project for Iris Lane, marking a significant infrastructure investment in the community.
cards.body:
The Vero Beach city government has given approval for a $190,000 sidewalk construction project on Iris Lane. The project represents a substantial infrastructure investment aimed at improving pedestrian safety and connectivity in the area.

The sidewalk construction is part of ongoing efforts by the city to enhance walkability and provide safer routes for residents traveling on foot. Iris Lane will see new sidewalk infrastructure installed as part of the approved project.

The $190,000 price tag covers the full scope of construction and materials needed to complete the sidewalk installation. City officials approved the project during recent proceedings, moving the infrastructure improvement forward for the Vero Beach community.

cards.headline: Vero Beach to receive historical marker honoring Florida woman
cards.teaser: A historical marker will be installed in Vero Beach to commemorate a notable Florida woman, recognizing her contributions to the community and state history.
cards.body:
Vero Beach is set to receive a new historical marker commemorating a Florida woman whose impact on the community and state earned her this lasting recognition. The marker will serve as a permanent reminder of her contributions and legacy in the area.

Historical markers play an important role in preserving local history and educating residents and visitors about significant figures and events that shaped the community. The installation in Vero Beach continues this tradition of honoring those who made meaningful contributions to Florida history.

The marker will be placed in Vero Beach, providing a visible tribute to the woman being honored. Such commemorations help ensure that important local history is remembered and celebrated by future generations.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce Islamic Center marks 10 years since arson fire
cards.teaser: The Islamic Center of Fort Pierce is looking back at the arson fire that struck the facility a decade ago, reflecting on the community's recovery and resilience.
cards.body:
The Islamic Center of Fort Pierce is commemorating the 10th anniversary of an arson fire that damaged the facility. The incident, which occurred a decade ago, was a significant event in the local Muslim community's history.

The arson fire represented a challenging moment for the Islamic Center and its members. Over the past 10 years, the community has worked to recover from the incident and continue serving Fort Pierce area Muslims.

The anniversary provides an opportunity to reflect on how far the center and community have come since the fire. Looking back at the incident allows current and future members to understand an important chapter in the facility's history.

cards.headline: Air conditioning company employee accused of identity theft in Treasure Coast case
cards.teaser: An air conditioning company employee faces accusations of using an 87-year-old customer's personal information to make a down payment on a car.
cards.body:
An employee of an air conditioning company is accused of using the personal information of an 87-year-old customer to put a down payment on a vehicle. The alleged identity theft represents a serious breach of trust between a service provider and a vulnerable customer.

The case involves the unauthorized use of the elderly person's information for the employee's financial benefit. Identity theft targeting senior citizens is a particular concern for law enforcement and consumer protection agencies throughout the Treasure Coast region.

The incident highlights the importance of safeguarding personal information, especially for elderly residents who may be targeted by unscrupulous individuals with access to their homes and documents. The case is being investigated by local authorities.

cards.headline: Florida planner offers vision for managing growth across the state
cards.teaser: A Florida planner is sharing ideas about how growth can be managed across the state in ways that preserve communities and quality of life.
cards.body:
A Florida planner has presented ideas about managing growth in the state, arguing that development does not have to come at the expense of community character and environmental quality. The perspective comes as Florida continues to experience rapid population growth and development pressure.

The planner's vision addresses one of the most pressing challenges facing Florida communities, including those on the Treasure Coast where growth and development have significantly impacted the region. Finding ways to accommodate new residents while preserving what makes Florida communities attractive has become a central concern for local governments and residents.

The discussion about growth management is particularly relevant to Treasure Coast counties, which have seen substantial development in recent years. How local officials and planners approach future growth will shape the character of Martin, St. Lucie, and Indian River counties for decades to come.

cards.headline: Former Florida mayor announces run for city commission seat
cards.teaser: A former Florida mayor is seeking a return to public office by running for a city commission position.
cards.body:
A former Florida mayor has announced plans to run for a city commission seat, marking an attempted return to local government after previously serving as the city's top elected official. The candidate's previous experience as mayor provides name recognition and familiarity with city operations.

The move to run for city commission rather than mayor represents a different role in local government, with commissioners serving as part of the legislative body that sets policy and approves budgets. Former mayors who seek commission seats bring executive experience to what is primarily a legislative position.

The race will give voters an opportunity to decide whether they want the former mayor back in city government in a new capacity. Local elections for city commission seats typically focus on issues like development, infrastructure, public safety, and fiscal management.

cards.headline: Five hospitalized after multi-vehicle crash sparks fire on I-95 in Martin County
cards.teaser: Five people were hospitalized Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park sparked a vehicle fire. All northbound lanes were closed during the investigation.
cards.body:
Five people were hospitalized Monday night after a multi-vehicle crash on Interstate 95 in Martin County that also sparked a vehicle fire. The collision occurred just before 10 p.m. on northbound I-95 near Exit 101 and Halpatiokee Regional Park in Stuart. Martin County Fire Rescue responded to the scene, where they found one of the vehicles on fire, and crews quickly extinguished the flames.

Two people suffered traumatic injuries and were transported to the hospital, while three others sustained minor injuries and were also taken for medical treatment. All northbound lanes of I-95 were closed while law enforcement investigated the crash.

As of Tuesday morning, all lanes have reopened. The Florida Highway Patrol is investigating the crash.

cards.headline: Former St. Lucie County school bus driver faces additional charge as second victim comes forward
cards.teaser: Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie, was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 after a second victim came forward. He was initially arrested in March on charges of lewd and lascivious molestation.
cards.body:
A former St. Lucie County school bus driver is facing an additional charge after a second victim came forward in an ongoing investigation into allegations of inappropriate conduct with children. Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie, was arrested on a new battery charge May 28. This comes after his initial arrest March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age.

The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area. The case was referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6.

The St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward. Anyone with information can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at (772) 462-7300 or email CrimeTips@stluciesheriff.gov.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman loses home and irreplaceable photos of late son in lightning strike fire
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned home from church last month to find her Fort Pierce house on fire after a lightning strike. She lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable photos of her late son.
cards.body:
A Fort Pierce woman is displaced and calling for help after a lightning strike tore through her home last month, leaving her with broken windows, heavy damage, and almost nothing left. Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church when a utility worker stopped her outside. St. Lucie County District firefighters rushed to put out the flames after Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire.

Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son, who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds. Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home.

A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera said she is holding onto gratitude that she was not inside when the fire broke out. A GoFundMe has been set up to help Rivera rebuild.

cards.headline: Black bear spotted swimming through Port St. Lucie neighborhood waterway
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police shared video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission is monitoring the bear.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie police shared rare video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before exiting the water and running toward nearby homes, marking an unusual wildlife sighting along the Treasure Coast. The video, posted on the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Facebook page, shows the large black bear navigating through residential waters in what officials described as seasonal behavior for Florida's black bear population.

The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission Bear Management Program said they are monitoring the bear. If it does not move from the area on its own, bear biologists may set a trap to try and capture and relocate it. Port St. Lucie police stated that as Florida's black bears become more active this time of year in search of food, occasional sightings in residential neighborhoods can occur. According to the FWC, bear sightings remain rare throughout most of the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County regions, making Tuesday's Port St. Lucie encounter particularly noteworthy for local residents.

Wildlife officials emphasize specific protocols when encountering black bears in residential areas. If residents spot a bear, authorities recommend maintaining significant distance, never approaching the animal, and avoiding any attempts to feed it. Port St. Lucie police advise residents to keep children and pets away from bears and secure potential food sources including garbage, pet food, and bird seed around their properties. During unexpected bear encounters, officials stress remaining calm and avoiding running. Instead, residents should slowly back away while keeping the bear visible, speak in calm, firm tones, and ensure the animal has a clear escape route.

cards.headline: Sebastian finalizes annexation for Cresswind development
cards.teaser: Sebastian has completed the annexation process for properties related to the Cresswind development, bringing additional land into the city limits.
cards.body:
The city of Sebastian has finalized annexations for the Cresswind development, officially incorporating the properties into the municipal boundaries. The action represents the completion of a process that allows the development to move forward under city jurisdiction and services.

Cresswind is an active adult community brand developed by Kolter Homes that typically features age-restricted neighborhoods with resort-style amenities. The annexation brings the development parcels under Sebastian city planning and zoning authority, along with city utilities and services.

The completion of the annexation process marks a significant step in expanding Sebastian's tax base and residential development. City officials typically approve annexations when they can provide adequate services to the new territory and when the development aligns with comprehensive plan goals for growth and land use.

cards.headline: Florida mall partially demolished as redevelopment continues
cards.teaser: A Florida mall has undergone partial demolition, with archival photos showing the shopping center during its peak years of operation.
cards.body:
Demolition crews have partially torn down a Florida mall, marking the end of an era for a shopping center that once served as a community gathering place. Historical photos document the mall during its busiest years, showing the architecture and retail landscape that defined an earlier generation of shopping culture.

The demolition represents the ongoing transformation of traditional enclosed malls across Florida as shopping habits shift toward online retail and outdoor lifestyle centers. Many aging malls built in the 1970s and 1980s are being demolished or significantly redeveloped into mixed-use properties combining residential, office, and entertainment uses.

The partial demolition suggests a redevelopment plan is underway that may preserve portions of the structure while reimagining the site for modern uses. Mall redevelopments typically take several years to complete as developers work through planning, financing, and construction phases to transform large retail sites into new community assets.

cards.headline: Indian River County restaurant earns perfect health inspection while another fails
cards.teaser: One restaurant in Indian River County received a perfect score during recent health inspections, while another establishment failed to meet standards.
cards.body:
Health inspectors in Indian River County issued a perfect score to one restaurant while failing another during recent inspections. The inspections are part of routine monitoring conducted by the Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation to ensure restaurants maintain proper food safety and sanitation standards.

Restaurants in Florida receive unannounced inspections throughout the year, with inspectors checking for violations in food storage temperatures, employee hygiene, facility cleanliness, and proper handling procedures. A perfect score indicates no violations were found during the inspection, while a failure means critical violations were discovered that could pose immediate health risks to customers.

Restaurants that fail inspections must correct violations and pass a follow-up inspection before continuing operations. The Florida Department of Business and Professional Regulation publishes inspection reports online, allowing residents to review the food safety records of any licensed restaurant before dining. Regular inspections help protect public health by identifying and correcting unsafe food handling practices before illnesses occur.

cards.headline: Buc-ee's announces expansion to six new states
cards.teaser: The Texas-based Buc-ee's travel center chain is opening locations in six additional states, expanding its regional footprint.
cards.body:
Buc-ee's, the Texas-based chain known for massive travel centers with dozens of fuel pumps and extensive convenience store offerings, is expanding into six new states. The expansion represents significant growth for the company, which has built a devoted following for its clean facilities, barbecue, and beaver mascot.

Buc-ee's locations typically span tens of thousands of square feet and feature fresh food, merchandise, and immaculate restrooms that have become the company's trademark. The travel centers are destination stops rather than typical convenience stores, drawing customers who plan trips around visiting the locations.

The expansion into new states follows Buc-ee's successful growth beyond Texas into neighboring states in recent years. Each new location creates hundreds of jobs and often becomes a tourism draw in itself, with the company selecting sites along major interstate highways where they can serve long-distance travelers.

cards.headline: Buc-ee's announces Arizona location opening
cards.teaser: Buc-ee's is opening a location in Arizona soon, with details emerging about where the popular travel center chain is heading next.
cards.body:
The Buc-ee's travel center chain has confirmed it will open a location in Arizona, marking the company's expansion into the southwestern United States. The announcement builds anticipation for the signature large-format convenience store and fuel center known for its devoted customer base.

Buc-ee's has built a reputation for exceptionally large facilities that combine fuel, food service, and retail in locations strategically placed along major travel corridors. The company emphasizes cleanliness and customer service, with facilities often exceeding 50,000 square feet and featuring dozens of fuel pumps to minimize wait times.

The Arizona expansion represents Buc-ee's push into new regional markets beyond its Texas home base and recent southeastern locations. Each new Buc-ee's becomes a landmark along its highway corridor, often generating significant local economic activity and creating several hundred jobs during construction and operation.

cards.headline: Florida residents can vote for best burrito restaurant in statewide contest
cards.teaser: A poll is asking Florida residents to vote for the restaurant that serves the best burritos in their area.
cards.body:
Florida residents have the opportunity to vote in a contest identifying the best burrito restaurant in the state. The voting allows customers to weigh in on their favorite establishments for the popular Mexican dish.

Burrito restaurants range from national fast-casual chains to local taquerias and food trucks, each offering different styles and ingredients. The contest format engages customers in recognizing quality food service and helps highlight popular local establishments that might not have the marketing reach of larger chains.

Community voting contests for restaurant categories have become popular ways to identify local favorites and generate discussion about food quality and customer service. The results often introduce residents to highly rated restaurants they might not have tried, supporting local dining businesses through increased visibility and customer traffic.

hero.headline: Florida Legislature Approves Property Tax Cut Plan for November Ballot
hero.body:

Jacksonville-area leaders joined officials from other regions in voicing concerns about the proposal. The measure would need to pass with 60 percent voter approval to become part of the Florida Constitution.

Florida voters will make the final decision this November on whether to approve the property tax changes. The debate reflects ongoing tension between state-level tax policy and local government funding needs, an issue that has played out repeatedly in recent Florida legislative sessions as property values have increased statewide.

hero.headline: Martin County Sheriff arrests three in 'Operation Hammer Time' retail theft ring that hit Stuart hardware stores
hero.body:
The Martin County Sheriff's Office announced arrests in a major retail theft operation that targeted hardware stores across the Treasure Coast. Three men have been identified in connection with Operation Hammer Time, a burglary ring that hit at least 40 stores across 13 counties between December 2025 and April 2026, including Sewell Hardware in Stuart.

Major Ruben Romero said the suspects are Johnny Batista, 19; Roberto Hernandez-Castro, 39; and Roberto Aldana-Ferrera, 31. All three lived in Miami-Dade County and transported stolen goods back there to sell. The theft ring stole roughly $500,000 worth of property and caused significant damage to stores across Martin, St. Lucie, and Palm Beach counties. A fourth suspect, Maikell Fleitas, is deceased. Batista is currently in Martin County Jail after being arrested in February for vehicle theft, while Aldana-Ferrera is in custody in Georgia. A warrant has been issued for Hernandez-Castro's arrest.

Investigators say the crews used sledgehammers or other blunt objects to smash store windows and completed thefts within minutes, before police could arrive or alarms could be triggered. Hardware stores in Stuart, Fort Pierce, Jupiter, Lake Worth, Delray Beach, Boynton Beach, and West Palm Beach were targeted, as well as stores in Broward County. The first known theft connected to Batista occurred at Sewell Hardware in Stuart in December 2025.

Romero explained the broader impact of these crimes on local residents. "There's already inflation that we notice severely in our state, and the more they steal, the more damage they cause, the more expensive things are," he said. "People can't go to work because they can't afford the tools." The suspects face charges including racketeering, burglary over $1,000 in damage while masked, burglary of an occupied structure, and burglary of an unoccupied structure. Investigators say there are burglaries that occurred before December and they are still looking for one additional suspect.

hero.body:
Jose Tsu Zamora, 64, of North Miami faces multiple felony charges following the incident at First United Methodist Church on Southwest Prima Vista Boulevard Sunday morning. The attempted kidnapping unfolded around 10:49 a.m. in the church parking lot, according to the Port St. Lucie Police Department. Zamora, who previously had a romantic relationship with the victim, approached the 74-year-old woman despite an active injunction prohibiting any contact with her.

Police say Zamora, while armed with a handgun, grabbed the victim by her arms and attempted to force her into his vehicle against her will. Several witnesses saw the incident and immediately intervened. Two Good Samaritans confronted Zamora and ordered him to release the victim. During the confrontation, Zamora displayed his firearm before retreating to his vehicle and fleeing the scene. Church surveillance footage captured portions of the encounter and corroborated witness statements, showing Zamora pursuing the victim through the parking lot and physically restraining her.

Zamora was located and arrested without incident Sunday evening at a residence in Hialeah by Port St. Lucie Police and U.S. Marshals. The investigation revealed Zamora is a convicted felon who is prohibited from possessing firearms or ammunition. Zamora faces five felony charges, including attempted kidnapping with a firearm, aggravated assault and battery of a person over 65. He is being held at St. Lucie County Jail on a $745,000 bond.

cards.headline: Former St. Lucie County school bus driver faces second molestation charge as victim comes forward
cards.teaser: Edwin Garcia, 72, of Port St. Lucie was arrested on a new battery charge May 28 when a second victim came forward, adding to the two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation he already faces from his March arrest.
cards.body:
The former St. Lucie County school bus driver was initially arrested March 6 on two counts of lewd and lascivious molestation of a victim under 12 years of age. The investigation began March 4 when a school resource deputy received a report that Garcia had allegedly asked a 9-year-old student to lift her dress while riding the school bus. During the preliminary investigation, deputies developed additional information suggesting Garcia may have made inappropriate comments to the child and possibly pinched her over her clothing in the pelvic area, according to the St. Lucie County Sheriff's Office.

The case was referred to the Criminal Investigations Division, leading to Garcia's initial arrest two days later on March 6. The Sheriff's Office continues to investigate the allegations and is encouraging anyone who may have been a victim or has additional information to come forward.

Anyone with information related to this case can contact Detective Corporal Hunter Limb at (772) 462-7300 or email CrimeTips@stluciesheriff.gov. The ongoing investigation suggests there may be additional victims from Garcia's time as a school bus driver in St. Lucie County.

cards.headline: Black bear spotted swimming through Port St. Lucie neighborhood waterway
cards.teaser: Port St. Lucie police shared rare video footage Tuesday of a black bear swimming through a waterway in the Town Park community before exiting the water and running toward nearby homes.
cards.body:
The video, posted on the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Facebook page, shows the large black bear navigating through residential waters in what officials described as seasonal behavior for Florida's black bear population. The Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission Bear Management Program said they are monitoring the bear. If it doesn't move from the area on its own, they said their bear biologists may set a trap to try and capture and relocate it.

Port St. Lucie police stated on Facebook that as Florida's black bears become more active this time of year in search of food, occasional sightings in residential neighborhoods can occur. While seeing a bear may be surprising, it is not necessarily cause for alarm, police said. According to the FWC, bear sightings remain rare throughout most of the Treasure Coast and Palm Beach County regions, making Tuesday's Port St. Lucie encounter particularly noteworthy for local residents.

Wildlife officials emphasize specific protocols when encountering black bears in residential areas. If residents spot a bear, authorities recommend maintaining significant distance, never approaching the animal, and avoiding any attempts to feed it. Port St. Lucie police advise residents to keep children and pets away from bears and secure potential food sources including garbage, pet food, and bird seed around their properties. During unexpected bear encounters, officials stress remaining calm and avoiding running. Instead, residents should slowly back away while keeping the bear visible, speak in calm, firm tones, and ensure the animal has a clear escape route.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman displaced after lightning strike destroys home, loses photos of late son
cards.teaser: Rosa Rivera returned home from getting a haircut at church last month to find a utility worker telling her that her house was on fire after a lightning strike.
cards.body:
St. Lucie County District Firefighters rushed to put out the flames. Rivera was told a lightning strike caused the fire. Walking into her damaged home left her stunned. Rivera lost clothes, furniture and irreplaceable personal belongings including photos of her late son who passed away three years ago. The damage left Rivera displaced. She is uninsured and is now staying at her nephew's home while she rebuilds.

Rivera, who is also disabled, was recovering from neck fusion surgery the same week she lost her home. A memorial outside the damaged home is one of the few things Rivera has left that cannot be replaced. Despite everything, Rivera said she is holding onto one thing: gratitude that she was not inside when the fire broke out.

A GoFundMe has been set up to help Rivera rebuild. The Fort Pierce woman faces a long recovery as she works to replace what was lost and find permanent housing. Her nephew has provided temporary shelter during this difficult time.

cards.headline: Historic Fort Pierce Boston House reopens as downtown dining destination
cards.teaser: The Boston House, a downtown Fort Pierce staple for more than a century, has officially reopened as a new dining experience, bringing fresh energy to a city working to redefine its future.
cards.body:
Built in 1909 along South Indian River Drive, the home is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and has served a variety of roles over the decades. Now, its newest owners are working to preserve its past while reimagining its purpose. Co-owner Georgette Angelos said Fort Pierce is eclectic, artistic, with deep, beautiful history. Behind its historic doors, the goal is simple: make guests feel at home while honoring the building's legacy.

Originally built by an engineer for Henry Flagler's Florida East Coast Railway, who later became St. Lucie County's third sheriff, the Boston House remains closely tied to the region's early development. During renovations, the owners intentionally preserved historic details, including low original ceilings and Florida-themed law books that nod to the home's past. General manager Scott Laird said the revival of the property reflects broader momentum downtown. Fort Pierce has had a reputation, and they really have done a great job bringing new life to the downtown area, Laird said.

Each room in the Boston House offers a distinct experience rooted in local history, blending preservation with a modern dining atmosphere. Laird emphasized the importance of holding onto the greatness in the area and shining a spotlight on it. The Boston House now stands as both a historic landmark and a renewed gathering place serving up a new chapter for downtown Fort Pierce.

cards.headline: St. Lucie County Fire District honors firefighter Connor Whitehead after his death
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie County Fire District held a ceremony to honor firefighter Connor Whitehead following his death.
cards.body:
The St. Lucie County Fire District gathered to pay tribute to firefighter Connor Whitehead in a ceremony honoring his service to the community. The event brought together fellow firefighters, department officials, and community members to remember Whitehead's dedication and sacrifice.

Whitehead served the St. Lucie County community as a member of the Fire District, responding to emergencies and protecting residents throughout the area. The ceremony highlighted his commitment to public service and the impact he made during his time with the department. Fire District personnel and local officials participated in the tribute, recognizing Whitehead's contributions to the safety and wellbeing of St. Lucie County residents.

The memorial service provided an opportunity for the community to come together and honor one of their own who dedicated his life to protecting others. The St. Lucie County Fire District continues to serve the community while remembering the legacy of firefighter Connor Whitehead.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie woman charged with attempted murder after setting fire with mother inside
cards.teaser: A 26-year-old Port St.
cards.body:
A 26-year-old Port St. Lucie woman is facing attempted murder and arson charges after allegedly setting fire to a bedroom door while her 62-year-old mother was trapped inside Sunday night. Michelle Picard was arrested following the incident at a home in the 1500 block of Southeast Airoso Boulevard, where Port St. Lucie police responded to reports of a domestic disturbance and active house fire around 9:05 p.m.

According to the Port St. Lucie Police Department, the victim first noticed smoke coming from underneath her bedroom door and discovered Picard standing nearby when she opened it. When the victim attempted to retrieve a fire extinguisher, Picard allegedly physically attacked her and tried to prevent her from putting out the fire. Police say Picard made threatening statements and attempted to push the victim toward the flames. The victim managed to escape to a bathroom, lock the door, and call 911. During the emergency call, Picard could be heard banging on the bathroom door in the background.

Officers found Picard outside the residence and detained her. She resisted arrest, causing injuries to one officer's leg and requiring another officer to receive treatment for smoke inhalation. Both officers were treated at a local hospital and released. The victim was also hospitalized for treatment of injuries sustained during the incident. Picard was taken to a hospital for medical evaluation before being cleared and transported to jail.

Fire investigators from the Port St. Lucie Police Department's Crime Scene unit, St. Lucie County Fire District, and the State Fire Marshal's Office determined the blaze was intentionally set. Picard faces charges of attempted murder, arson and resisting arrest without violence, with a total bond amount of $510,000. The fire damaged the residence, prompting the American Red Cross to assist the victim with temporary housing and support services. Police emphasized this was an isolated domestic incident and there is no ongoing threat to the community.

hero.headline: Indian River Mall demolition underway in Vero Beach, former Macy's store comes down
hero.body:
Demolition has begun at Indian River Mall in Vero Beach, with the former Macy's anchor store being the first major structure to come down. The partial demolition marks a significant transformation for the shopping center that has served the community for decades.

The mall redevelopment represents one of the most substantial commercial real estate projects currently underway in Indian River County. The demolition of the Macy's building clears the way for what developers envision as a reimagined shopping and entertainment destination for the Treasure Coast.

Photos from the mall's heyday show bustling crowds and thriving retail activity that defined the shopping experience for generations of Vero Beach residents. The mall has been a fixture of the local retail landscape, and its transformation reflects broader changes in how communities shop and gather.

Plans for the new Indian River Mall show a modernized layout designed to attract both retailers and visitors in a changing commercial environment. The redevelopment aims to bring new businesses and amenities to the property while preserving its role as a gathering place for the community.

cards.headline: World War II veteran Bill Keegan celebrates 102nd birthday in Indian River County with motorcycle ride
cards.teaser: A local World War II veteran marked his 102nd birthday in style this week, taking a motorcycle ride to celebrate the milestone.
cards.body:
Bill Keegan, a World War II veteran living in Indian River County, celebrated his 102nd birthday with a motorcycle ride. The centenarian's birthday celebration highlights the dwindling number of World War II veterans still living in the community and honors their service.

The motorcycle ride provided a fitting celebration for Keegan, who has now lived more than a century. Veterans like Keegan represent a direct connection to one of the most significant periods in American history, and their presence in the community offers younger generations a chance to hear firsthand accounts of the war.

As the Greatest Generation continues to age, communities across the Treasure Coast have increasingly recognized the importance of honoring these veterans while they are still with us. Keegan's active lifestyle at 102 demonstrates the resilience and spirit that characterized his generation.

cards.headline: Vero Beach approves $190,000 for Iris Lane sidewalk construction
cards.teaser: The city of Vero Beach has approved funding for a new sidewalk project on Iris Lane, addressing pedestrian safety and connectivity.
cards.body:
Vero Beach officials approved a $190,000 expenditure for sidewalk construction on Iris Lane. The project will add pedestrian infrastructure to an area that currently lacks safe walking paths for residents.

Sidewalk projects like this one are part of ongoing efforts to improve walkability and safety throughout Vero Beach neighborhoods. Many older residential areas in the city were developed without sidewalks, leaving pedestrians to walk in streets or along road shoulders.

The Iris Lane project reflects the city's commitment to upgrading infrastructure in established neighborhoods. Construction timelines and specific details about the sidewalk's length and route will be determined as the project moves forward.

cards.headline: Indian River County commissioners continue review of Racquet Club development request
cards.teaser: County commissioners are continuing their deliberations on a development proposal for the Racquet Club property in Indian River County.
cards.body:
Indian River County commissioners have continued their review of a development request involving the Racquet Club property. The ongoing deliberations indicate that officials are taking time to carefully consider the proposal's impacts on the surrounding area.

Development requests in Indian River County often draw significant community interest, particularly when they involve changes to established recreational facilities or neighborhood character. The Racquet Club proposal is working its way through the county's review process, which includes assessments of land use compatibility, traffic impacts, and community concerns.

County commissioners will continue their evaluation of the project before making a final decision. The development review process allows for public input and ensures that proposed projects align with the county's comprehensive plan and zoning regulations.

cards.headline: Historical marker unveiled in Vero Beach honoring notable Florida woman
cards.teaser: A new historical marker has been installed in Vero Beach to commemorate a significant figure in Florida history.
cards.body:
Vero Beach has commemorated a notable Florida woman with a new historical marker. The installation recognizes her contributions and preserves her legacy for future generations visiting the area.

Historical markers serve an important educational function in communities, highlighting significant people, places, and events that shaped local and state history. The Vero Beach marker adds to the network of such commemorations throughout Indian River County and provides residents and visitors with insight into the area's past.

The marker installation reflects ongoing efforts to recognize diverse historical figures and tell a more complete story of Florida's development. These commemorations help connect current residents to the people and events that shaped their community.

cards.headline: Boaters rescued by Good Samaritan after boat sinks in Indian River Lagoon
cards.teaser: A group of boaters was pulled to safety after their vessel sank in the Indian River Lagoon, thanks to quick action by a nearby boater.
cards.body:
Multiple boaters were rescued from the Indian River Lagoon after their boat sank. A Good Samaritan who witnessed the sinking pulled the boaters to safety before the vessel went under completely.

One of those rescued expressed gratitude for the outcome, noting that everyone made it to safety. The incident serves as a reminder of the importance of boater preparedness and the value of nearby vessels keeping watch for distressed boaters on the water.

The Indian River Lagoon sees heavy recreational boating traffic, and incidents like this highlight both the risks of being on the water and the willingness of fellow boaters to help in emergencies. Boaters are encouraged to ensure their vessels are in good working order and to carry proper safety equipment before heading out on the lagoon.

cards.headline: Florida Margaritaville specialty license plate wins national award
cards.teaser: A Florida specialty license plate featuring the Margaritaville theme has received national recognition for its design.
cards.body:
The Florida Margaritaville specialty license plate has won an award, bringing recognition to the state's popular themed tag program. The plate is available for Florida drivers to purchase as an alternative to standard license plates.

Florida offers dozens of specialty license plates that allow drivers to show support for causes, organizations, or themes while generating revenue for associated programs. The Margaritaville plate joins other popular specialty tags in the state's diverse offering.

Residents interested in obtaining the Margaritaville plate can order it through the standard specialty plate process. Specialty plates typically involve an additional fee beyond standard registration costs, with a portion of the proceeds supporting designated programs or causes.
